Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:10:1.hebrew: נותנין לו ז' ימי המשתה - דלא חזי ליה, דלמא מטמא ליה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:10:1.english: We give him the seven days of the feast - That [the priest] does not examine him, lest he declare him impure.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:10:2.english: And for his garment - If the leprous mark appeared on his garment.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:11:1.hebrew: אם ממתינין לדבר הרשות - הרי ממתינין לו שאין מטמאין עד שמפנה כל הכלים שבבית, וילפי' מינה דבטומאה דבגופיה נמי ממתין לדבר הרשות דומיא דהכא. כיון דאשכחן דבטומאה דגופיה ממתינין לו לדבר הרשות, כ"ש דממתינין לו לדבר מצוה, כגון חתן וברגל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:11:1.english: If we delay for an optional matter - Behold, we wait for him, for they do not declare [the house] impure until he removes all the utensils that are in the house, and we derive from it that regarding impurity of his body as well, [the priest] waits for an optional matter, similar to here. Since we have found that regarding impurity of his body we wait for him for an optional matter, all the more so do we wait for him for a matter of mitzvah, such as a bridegroom or during a Festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:12:1.hebrew: משמעות דורשין - דמר דריש מהאי קרא, ומר דריש מהאי קרא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:12:1.english: The interpretation of [those] expounding - For one [Sage] expounds [it] from this verse, and the other [Sage] expounds [it] from that verse.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:12:2.hebrew: דבר הרשות איכא בינייהו - רבי יהודה דמפיק מביום הראות בו, ומכאן אמרו: חתן ורגל — דהיינו מצוה — ממתינין לו, אבל לדבר הרשות אין ממתינין לו בטומאה דגופיה. ורבי סבר דבדבר רשות נמי ממתינין לו, כדאמרי' לעיל, דרבי יליף טומאה דגופיה להמתין לו מטומאה דביתו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:12:2.english: An optional matter is [the difference] between them - Rabbi Yehuda, who derives [the law] from "on the day [it] is seen in him" [Leviticus 13:14], and from here they said [regarding] a groom and a festival — which is a mitzvah — [that] we wait for him, but for an optional matter we do not wait for him regarding the impurity of his body. Whereas Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] holds that for an optional matter as well we wait for him, as we said above, for Rabbi derives [the law of] the impurity of his body, to wait for him, from the impurity of his house.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:13:1.hebrew: לא גמרינן - דהוי חידוש, ומחידוש לא ילפינן, דכל היכא דאיכא חידוש אין לך דבר בו אלא חידושו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:13:1.english: We do not learn - because it is a novelty, and from a novelty we do not derive [other laws], for wherever there is a novelty, you have nothing in it except its novelty.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:1.hebrew: בהסגר שני - דאי מטמא ליה, מחליט ליה בטומאה חמורה ומצער ליה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:1.english: In [the] second quarantine - For if [the priest] declares him impure, he confirms him [as a leper] with severe impurity and distresses him.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:2.hebrew: מר - ר"מ, דאמר רואה להקל, לטהר אבל לא לטמא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:2.english: One Sage - Rabbi Meir, who says [that the priest] examines [the mark] to be lenient, to declare [it] pure, but not to declare [it] impure.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:3.hebrew: סבר בכהן תלא רחמנא - דאי מטמא ליה הוי טמא, ואי לא בעי מטמא ליה לא הוי טמא. ולהכי חזי ליה להקל אבל לא להחמיר, דאי חזי ליה דהוי טמא, לא לימא ליה כלום ולא הוי טמא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:3.english: He holds [that] the Merciful One made [it] dependent on the priest - For if he declares him impure, he is impure, and if he does not want to declare him impure, he is not impure. And therefore he examines him to be lenient, but not to be stringent; for if he sees that he is impure, he should not say anything to him, and he will not be impure.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:4.hebrew: ומר - ר' יוסי, דאמר לא להקל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:4.english: And [the other] master - [This is] Rabbi Yosei, who said not to be lenient.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:5.hebrew: סבר לטהרו ולטמאו כתיב - דכי חזי ליה כהן דטמא, לא מצי למשתק, ודלמא הוי טמא, ונמצא מצערו שמטמאו במועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:1:5.english: [And one Sage] holds: "to pronounce it pure and to pronounce it impure" is written - For when the priest sees that he is impure, he cannot remain silent; and perhaps he is impure, and thus [the priest] ends up distressing him by declaring him impure on the festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:2:1.hebrew: והא תניא איפכא - דברי ר"מ במוחלט, דברי ר' יוסי במוסגר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:2:1.english: But isn't the opposite taught - The words of Rabbi Meir [apply] regarding a confirmed [leper], [and] the words of Rabbi Yosei regarding a quarantined [leper].

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:3:1.hebrew: ומר סבר צוותא דעלמא עדיף ליה - האי תנא, דאמר א"ר נראין דברי ר"מ במוחלט ודברי ר' יוסי במוסגר, סבר צוותא דעלמא עדיף ליה, ולהכי חזי בימי חלוטו: דאי מטמאו, לא מטמא יותר מדמעיקרא, ואי מטהרו, משמחו דאית ליה צוותא דעלמא — אף על גב דאסור בתשמיש המטה, צוותא דעלמא עדיף ליה. ודברי רבי יוסי במוסגר, דלא חזי ליה, דלמא מטמא ליה חוץ לג' מחנות, ולית ליה צוותא דעלמא ומצער ליה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:3:1.english: And one Sage holds that the company of the world is preferable to him - This Tanna, who said: "Rabbi said: The words of Rabbi Meir appear [correct] regarding a confirmed [leper], and the words of Rabbi Yose regarding a quarantined [leper]," holds [that] the company of the world is preferable to him, and therefore [the priest] examines [him] during the days of his confirmation [as a leper]. For if he declares him impure, he does not become more impure than before; and if he declares him pure, he gladdens him, since he has the company of the world — even though he is [still] forbidden in marital relations, the company of the world is preferable to him. And the words of Rabbi Yose [apply] to a quarantined [leper], that [the priest] does not examine him, lest he declare him impure [and send him] outside the three camps, and he will not have the company of the world, and it will distress him.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:4:1.hebrew: מר סבר צוותא דאשתו עדיף ליה - ולהכי חזי ליה במועד בהסגר שני, דאי מטהרו משמחו, ואפי' מטמא ליה ומחליט ליה ומשדר ליה חוץ מג' מחנות, ולית ליה צוותא דאינשי דעלמא, אפ"ה לית ליה צערא, דהא אית ליה צוותא דאשתו, ומותר הוא באשתו להתיחד עמה בימי חלוטו. ודברי ר' יוסי במוחלט, דאפי' מטהר ליה, דאע"ג דשרי ליה למחנה ישראל, אית ליה צערא דלית ליה צוותא דאשתו, דאסור הוא; דכיון דמטהר ליה מחלוטו, מיבעי ליה למימני שבע ימי ספירו, ובימי ספירו אסור בתשמיש המטה, דכתיב: "וישב מחוץ לאהלו שבעת ימים", ואהלו זו אשתו, דכתיב: "שובו לכם לאהליכם":
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:4:1.english: One Sage holds [that] the company of his wife is preferable to him - And therefore he [the priest] examines him on the Festival during the second quarantine, for if he declares him pure, he gladdens him; and even if he declares him impure and confirms him [as a leper] and sends him outside of [the] three camps, and he does not have the company of ordinary people, even so he has no distress, for behold, he has the company of his wife, and he is permitted to his wife to be secluded with her during the days of his confirmed [leprosy]. And the words of Rabbi Yose [refer] to a confirmed [leper], that even [if] he declares him pure — for although he is permitted [to enter] the camp of Israel, he has distress because he does not have the company of his wife, as he is forbidden [to her]; for once he declares him pure from his confirmed [leprosy], he must count the seven days of his counting [period], and during the days of his counting he is forbidden marital relations, as it is written: "and he shall dwell outside his tent seven days," and "his tent" — this is his wife, as it is written: "Return to your tents."

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:5:1.hebrew: ימי ספירו - אסור בתשמיש המטה, ולא ימי חלוטו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:5:1.english: The days of his counting - [He is] prohibited from conjugal relations, and not [during] the days of his confirmed [leprosy].

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:7:1.hebrew: יותם לא היה לעוזיהו אלא בימי חלוטו - כלומר, לא נתעברה אמו דיותם אלא בימי חלוטו דעוזיהו, דעוזיהו היה מצורע, ולא נזקק לאשתו בימי ספירו אלא בימי חלוטו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:7:1.english: Jotham was only [born] to Uzziah during the days of his confirmed [leprosy] - That is to say, Jotham's mother only conceived [him] during the days of Uzziah's confirmed [leprosy], for Uzziah was a leper, and he did not have marital relations with his wife during the days of his counting, only during the days of his confirmed [leprosy].

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:7:2.hebrew: אף אני כך אמרתי - דמצורע מותר בתשמיש המטה, דוישב מחוץ לאהלו בימי ספירו כתיב:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:7:2.english: I too said this - That a leper is permitted [to engage in] marital relations, for "and he shall dwell outside his tent" is written regarding the days of his counting.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:8:1.hebrew: ורבי סבר מאי דגלי גלי - להכי אמרי' ימי ספירו ולא ימי חלוטו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:8:1.english: And Rabbi holds: That which [the Torah] revealed, it revealed - For this reason we say [that conjugal relations are prohibited during] the days of his counting, and not [during] the days of his confirmed [leprosy].

Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:9:1.hebrew: למימרא דבכהן תליא מילתא - פריך בין לר"מ בין לרבי יוסי; דר"מ אומר בהדיא אי טמא שתיק, ורבי יוסי קאמר אין רואין כלל, מכלל דרבי יוסי סבר אי לא בעי לא חזי ליה ולא הוי טמא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7b:9:1.english: Is this to say that the matter depends upon the priest - [The Gemara] asks [this] according to both R. Meir and R. Yose: for R. Meir states explicitly [that] if he is impure, [the priest] remains silent, and R. Yose says [that] they do not examine [him] at all, which implies that R. Yose holds [that] if [the priest] does not want [to], he does not examine him, and he does not become impure.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:12:1.hebrew: משמעות דורשין איכא בינייהו - ר' דורש מופינו, וביום אצטריך למידרש ביום ולא בלילה, כדלקמן; וי"ו לא משמע ליה. ור' יהודה דורש מוביום, אבל ופינו את הבית — שמא אצטריך לרבי יהודה אפי' חבילי קש וחבילי עצים, כדתנן בנגעים (פ' י"ב מ"ה) לרבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:12:1.english: The interpretation of the meaning [of the verses] is [the difference] between them - Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] expounds [it] from "and they shall empty [the house]," and "and on the day" (uvayom) is needed to expound: by day and not by night, as [the Gemara states] below; the [letter] vav does not imply [anything additional] to him. And Rabbi Yehuda expounds [it] from "and on the day," whereas [as for] "and they shall empty the house" — perhaps it is needed for Rabbi Yehuda [to teach that one empties] even bundles of straw and bundles of wood, as we learned in [Tractate] Negaim (12:5) according to Rabbi Yehuda.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:12:2.hebrew: דבר הרשות איכא בינייהו - דרבי יהודה סבר חידוש הוא, ואין ללמוד הימנה שאר המתנות, ומ"ביום הראות בו" לא משמע אלא המתנה דמצוה, דמשמע דתלוי הדבר בקביעת היום, כגון רגל, והוא הדין לחתן; ורבי סבר לרבות נמי המתנה שאינה מצוה, וגמרינן שפיר להמתנה מ"ופינו". כל דבר הרשות בבית לא פליגי, דהא בהדיא כתיב "ופינו את הבית", אלא דבר הרשות דגופיה איכא בינייהו. ואין נראה לפרש שאר דברי רשות, כגון חבילי קש, ופליגי בבתים, דלרבי יהודה דאמר חידוש הוא לא ילפינן:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:12:2.english: An optional matter is [the difference] between them - For Rabbi Yehuda holds [that waiting to examine a house] is a novel ruling, and one cannot learn other delays from it, and from "on the day it appears in it" only a delay for a mitzvah is implied, as it implies that the matter depends on the fixed nature of the day, such as a festival, and the same applies to a groom; and Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] holds to also include a delay that is not a mitzvah, and we properly derive [such] a delay from "and they shall clear out." [Regarding] any optional matter in a house they do not disagree, for it is explicitly written "and they shall clear out the house," rather, an optional matter of his body is [the difference] between them. And it does not seem [correct] to explain [that it refers to] other optional matters, such as bundles of straw, and that they disagree regarding houses, [such] that according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says it is a novel ruling, we do not derive [them].

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:1:1.hebrew: לטהרו או לטמאו כתיב - בפ' בתרא דנזיר (דף סה: ושם) דריש מיניה: פתח הכתוב בטהרה תחילה, גבי ספק שער לבן קודם לבהרת. והתם דריש מדכתיב "לטהרו" ברישא, והכא דריש מגופיה דקרא:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:1:1.english: "To pronounce it pure or to pronounce it impure" is written - In the last chapter of Nazir (65b and there), [the Gemara] expounds from it [that] Scripture opened with purity first, regarding a doubt [as to whether] the white hair preceded the bright spot [baheret]. And there it expounds from [the fact] that "to pronounce it pure" is written first, whereas here it expounds from the body of the verse itself.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג בתורת כהנים: "שבעת ימים", ימי ספירו וכו' - ואגב שנכתב בפסוק בתר "ואחרי טהרתו וגו'", כתבוהו כאן:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:5:1.english: This is the reading in Torat Kohanim: "Seven days" — the days of his counting, etc. - And because [that phrase] is written in the verse after "and after his purification, etc." [in Ezekiel 44:26], they wrote it here [in the Gemara].

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:7:1.hebrew: יותם לא היה לו לעוזיהו אלא בימי חלוטו - פירש הר"ר קלונימוס: דכתיב (ישעיהו ז׳:ח׳) "ובעוד ששים וחמש שנה יחת אפרים מעם", והיינו מנבואת עמוס, אע"פ שישעיה אמרה; וישעיה נתנבא בשעה שנתנגע עוזיהו, כדמוכח קראי שהיה רעש ע"י שרעשו עליונים לשורפו ותחתונים לבלעו. הוא מונה לנבואת עמוס שנתנבא שנתים לפני הרעש: "וישראל גלה יגלה מעל אדמתו" (עמוס ז׳:י״א), שאז נגזרה גזירה. וכמה יש עד גלות הושע בן אלה שהיה בשנת שש לחזקיהו? חשבונו ס"ה שנים: ב' שנים קודם נגעו, וכ"ה דנגעו — דעוזיהו נתנגע כ"ה שנים לפני מותו — וי"ו דיותם, ושש עשרה דאחז, ושש לחזקיה היה הגלות, הרי ס"ה שנים. ויותם בן כ"ה שנים כשמלך, וא"כ היה עיבורו בימי חלוטו! מכל מקום אין ר' יוסי בר' יהודה מוקשה, די"ל דנתנגע בסוף השנה ועיבורו היתה בתחילת השנה. ובפי' נביאים פרש"י חשבון זה, וכן מוכיח בסדר עולם. ומאחר שזה אמת, נמצא שצריך ליישב: והלא עוזיהו וירבעם מלכו כאחת, דהא ירבעם מלך מ"א שנה, וא"כ כשמת היה מ"א למלכות עוזיהו, והכתוב אומר: "בשנת שלשים ושמנה לעזריה מלך יהודה מלך זכריה בן ירבעם", וא"כ חסר ג' שנים! וי"ל דמלך ג' שנים בחיי אביו; וכן הגיה במקצת פירושים, דהכי הוה מעשה, דזכריה מלך בחיי ירבעם אביו ג' שנים:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:7:1.english: Jotham was only [born] to Uzziah during the days of his confirmed [leprosy] - Rabbi Kalonymus explained: For it is written (Isaiah 7:8): "And within sixty-five years, Ephraim shall be shattered from being a people." And this [count] is from the prophecy of Amos, even though Isaiah said it. Now Isaiah prophesied at the time when Uzziah was afflicted with leprosy, as the verses demonstrate that there was an earthquake because the upper [realms] trembled to burn him and the lower [realms] to swallow him. He [Isaiah] counts from the prophecy of Amos, who prophesied two years before the earthquake: "And Israel shall surely be exiled from upon its land" (Amos 7:11), for then the decree was issued. And how much [time] is there until the exile of Hoshea son of Elah, which was in the sixth year of Hezekiah? Its calculation is sixty-five years: two years before his leprosy, and twenty-five of his leprosy — for Uzziah was afflicted with leprosy twenty-five years before his death — sixteen of Jotham, and sixteen of Ahaz, and [in the] sixth [year] of Hezekiah was the exile; behold, sixty-five years. And Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and if so, his conception was during the days of his [father's] confirmed [leprosy]! Nevertheless, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, is not challenged [by this], for one can say that he was afflicted with leprosy at the end of the year, whereas his conception was at the beginning of the year. And in his commentary on the Prophets, Rashi explained this calculation, and so it is proven in Seder Olam. And since this is true, it follows that one must reconcile [a difficulty]: Did not Uzziah and Jeroboam begin to reign together? For Jeroboam reigned forty-one years, and if so, when he died it was the forty-first [year] of Uzziah's reign; yet Scripture states: "In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king," and if so, three years are missing! And one can say that he reigned three years during the lifetime of his father; and so it was emended in some commentaries, that such was the incident, that Zechariah reigned during the lifetime of Jeroboam his father for three years.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:8:1.hebrew: מאי דלא גלי לא גלי - יש מקשין: למה אין רבי דורש ק"ו, הא אדם דן ק"ו מעצמו? ושמא יש שם פירכא, או שמא מצורע חידוש הוא; א"נ, "ז' ימים" משמע מיעוט, לאפוקי ימי חלוטו. ואידך — דמצטריך לגופיה; מיהו מדכתיב ביה "לו", שמע מינה למעוטי:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:8:1.english: That which it did not reveal, it did not reveal - Some ask: Why does Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] not expound an a fortiori inference, [given that] a person may expound an a fortiori inference on his own? [One may answer that] perhaps there is a refutation there [to the inference], or perhaps [the law of] a leper is an anomaly [from which one cannot derive further laws]. Alternatively, "seven days" implies a limitation, to exclude the days of his confirmed [leprosy]. And the other [Sage holds] that [the phrase "seven days"] is needed for itself. However, from the fact that it is written in it "for him," we learn from this [that it comes] to exclude [the days of confirmed leprosy].

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:9:1.hebrew: יש יום שאי אתה רואה בו - תימה לר"מ: למה אינו רואה להקל? ועוד, למאי דפי' רבינו יצחק דלכולי עלמא בתחילת הסגר רואין להקל, לעולם יכול לראות. ועוד: ופינו את הבית עד שיראו — למה טורח לפנות, שמא ימצא טהור:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7b:9:1.english: "There is a day when you do not examine him" - It is astonishing to Rabbi Meir: why does he not examine [him] to be lenient? And furthermore, according to what Rabbeinu Yitzchak explained, that according to everyone, at the beginning of a quarantine we examine [the person] to be lenient, he can always examine [him]. And furthermore, [regarding] "And they shall clear out the house" before they examine [it] — why does he trouble [himself] to clear [it] out, [since] perhaps it will be found pure?
